method: Read each exact Gujarati block and corresponding English original; reverse-paraphrase important scope/direction/definition/proof distinctions.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A binary relation on A is a subset of A squared. Rxy and xRy abbreviate ordered-pair membership, without exchanging coordinates.
samples.assessment: Definition, base set, direction and equivalence retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If membership denotes merely a set, the expression has three names and lacks a predicate able to express a proposition. Treating membership as a predicate is the proviso.
samples.assessment: Preserves use/mention distinction and the argument rather than endorsing its premise.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The membership relation would have to be the set of all x,y with x in y; its existence is not automatic. An axiomatic set theory denies that set.
samples.assessment: Both conditional branches and footnote kept. Reader selects upstream absent-chapter alternative.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Antisymmetry only permits both directions when the relata are equal. It neither requires all diagonal pairs nor means merely not symmetric. Identity can be symmetric and antisymmetric.
samples.assessment: Universal/conditional scope and distinction from asymmetry retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Given Rxy and Rxz, symmetry gives Ryx and transitivity gives Ryz. Thus the class of x is contained in the class of y; the reverse inclusion gives equality.
samples.assessment: Proof uses symmetry before transitivity, preserving correct orientation.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For the enlarged relation, two old edges compose by transitivity; if one edge is diagonal, substitute the equal endpoints. All cases yield the enlarged x,z edge.
samples.assessment: All cases retained; no assumption of old-relation reflexivity.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Divisibility is a partial order on natural numbers but only a preorder on integers, since 1 and minus 1 divide one another.
samples.assessment: Natural/integer base domains and nonlinearity examples kept distinct.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A graph explicitly specifies its vertex set and may include isolated vertices. The same edge relation can therefore yield different graphs on different vertex sets.
samples.assessment: Both diagrams retain self-loop and isolated-vertex distinction.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Each nonroot node has at most one immediate predecessor, not necessarily an immediate predecessor.
samples.assessment: At-most-one preserved; no finite-tree condition silently imposed on general trees.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A branch is an inclusion-maximal chain; every omitted vertex has an incomparable vertex in the chain.
samples.assessment: Maximality clarified as inclusion, not longest chain. Undefined X retained from source and flagged separately.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An infinite tree with finitely many immediate successors at every node has an infinite branch.
samples.assessment: Both infinitude and finite branching are essential and retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The relative product follows R from x to y, then S from y to z. Restriction intersects both coordinates with A squared.
samples.assessment: Composition order and two-coordinate restriction preserved; not function-only domain restriction.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Positive finite successor iterations on the integers give strict less-than; adjoining identity gives less-than-or-equal.
samples.assessment: R+ versus R* distinction and n at least one retained.
